I am a recruiter in the technical field and have spoken to hundreds of interviewers looking for a job. here are some pointers that are easy and make a lot of impact :

  • Be on time.

  • Dress as a professional (better to be overdressed then underdressed)

  • Have a professional e-mail address (not like farthugger99 or hellraiserz1988, I still see these a lot)

  • Have a proper CV and bring a printed version to you interview. (They will have a copy printed out themselves, but it looks good when you walk trough it)

  • Do your homework, read about the company your visiting, look at the linkedin page of the person you are meeting etc etc.

  • Bring a pen and piece of paper. (write down some notes during the interview, makes the employer feel like he's saying useful things)

  • Think of 5 - 10 questions related to the company or job. (ask them about their experiences with the company and future prospects)

  • Try to be yourself and be open and honest. (lies or "putting on an act" will surface in the long run or during your trial period)

  • Be positive and don't "bad mouth" earlier employers.

  • Be polite and use correct terms and speak correctly.

  • Open with a firm handshake and look the other in the eyes.

Most important advise if you fail; keep going to interviews, they will get easier, your tension will go down and the experience in these meetings will start to scale

I can't emphasize enough about dressing professionally. I've conducted interview of all sorts and had people show up in anything from a tshirt and jeans to shorts and flip flops. It just resonates how seriously you're taking it.

Also questions. Every interview I've ever been in always asked if I had any questions and not having any can be a sign of dealing with someone who might not know what they're getting into. Which just ties into doing you're homework about the job and place of work. Glass door is a mixed bag but can help get a feel for a company as well as Linkedin.
